message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "The azygos vein has been displaced medially, leaving the fissure empty and the opacity absent.", "reason": "The teardrop-shaped opacity at the caudal end of the azygos fissure corresponds to the azygos vein. In the setting of pneumothorax and chest tube placement (as shown in Figure 3a), increased intrathoracic pressure or mediastinal shift can displace the azygos vein medially away from its normal position within the fissure, causing the characteristic opacity to disappear from that location. This is a known radiographic sign associated with tension physiology or significant mediastinal displacement, rather than resolution of effusion or collapse of the vein itself."}
